profile.org_note: Since August 2026 Highland runs a division-led structure: three divisions (Dallas-Fort Worth; Houston under Jarod Mouton; Central Texas = Austin + San Antonio under John DePasquale), with local functional teams reporting to the Division President, under Chairman and CEO Aaron Graham. Land decisions sit with Chief Strategy and Land Officer Jeff Stinson, supported by a VP of Land and market Land Acquisitions Managers; the CFO is not confirmed by a primary source. The founders Rod Sanders and Jean Ann Brock remain directors/managers of every entity; the company is owned by an ESOP.
profile.summary: Employee-owned (ESOP) Texas builder, founded 1985 in Plano by Rod Sanders and Jean Ann Brock, building roughly 3,000 to 3,500 homes a year in Dallas-Fort Worth, Houston, Austin and San Antonio, historically on finished lots in third-party master plans. In 2026 it began self-developing land (Heritage Bend in Fulshear with Hines; a 100-acre Melina tract in Georgetown) and reorganised into division-led operations after President/COO Tony Marchbanks left. Brands: Highland Homes, Huntington Homes (luxury) and HHS Residential (build-to-rent).

people.name: Jeff Stinson
people.title: Chief Strategy and Land Officer
people.prior_role: Senior Vice President of Land and Strategic Planning (quoted July 2026); earlier Senior Vice President of Land
people.source_title: Builder and Developer: Highland Homes announces restructuring
people.note: Top land executive and the first call for a land banker. Promoted in the August 2026 restructuring to lead enterprise strategy and land initiatives. Spokesman for Highland's new self-development push: the 188-acre, 554-home Heritage Bend parcel in Fulshear (Hines master plan; Highland doing horizontal development, first 204 homesites early 2027) and a 100-acre, ~400-lot Melina tract in Georgetown (myneighborhoodnews.com 2026-07-22; bdmag.com 2026-08-13, which still used his older SVP of Land title). Reporting line inferred from title.
